title: Colors — Chromatic Chapters
subtitle: Yellow, blue, and red organizing distinct practical actions without recoloring
lineage: Lineage: Daniel Mercadante / The Mercadantes, Colors
theorem: Use recurring color to carry attention across unrelated settings, then reveal that the same hue can organize very different actions. No artificial color grading is applied to force a match.
boundary_note: All hues are native to the archival transfers and verified by HSV dominant-hue inspection; no synthetic recoloring is used.

v1_defect_timecodes: Seg #02 (t=03.50s-08.70s): `676ac70c` (`Skateboard Sense`) shows a dark green work glove rather than yellow.
Seg #06 (t=24.70s-30.50s): `029b1dea` (`Make Art Feel Better`) shows beige wood whittling with almost no blue present.
critic_tribunal.largest_gap: The opening anchor of Chapter I: Yellow features a green glove, and Seg #06 in Chapter II: Blue is visually dominated by beige wood shavings.
critic_tribunal.causal_hypothesis: Lack of HSV dominant-hue verification on candidate frames in Seg #02 and Seg #06.
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: Replace Seg #02 with HSV-verified yellow industrial work clip `56cdd913` (`1.5s-6.8s`, 41.4% yellow pixels) alongside `da09f0cb` (`Automatic Emergency Parking Brake`) and `43d553f4` (`Winter Alert`); replace Seg #06 in Chapter II: Blue with verified blue-screen/mist clips `45680277` (`2.2s-7.8s`) and `005ac24d` (`2.5s-8.0s`).
critic_tribunal.strength_to_preserve: The Chapter I -> II mixed-color transition bridge in `43d553f4` (`Winter Alert`, where a blue-sleeved arm latches a worn yellow machine door) and the two quiet red practical actions in Chapter III (`04572067`, `0f500d93`).
